features.name: The mutation drill - 16 arms (NO COMMIT; tree restored byte-identical)
features.description: Land, read, restore and sha-verify MU1-MU16. This is the sprint's spine: the five laws are Z3-proven but Z3 is BLIND to a consistent lie, so the named runtime identities are the only thing that kills 'silence synthesizes execution' (MU2) and 'an early timeout is legal' (MU14). The milestone's deliverable is EVIDENCE, not a diff: at exit every touched file is byte-identical to COMMIT 1.
mutation_protocol: 1. Backup exists in /tmp/w15_backup/ (cp, made in M1.0). Record the pre sha256.
2. Apply with a replacement that ASSERTS its exact occurrence count (1 for body-only, 2 for 'both'). A sed that silently matched nothing is the failure this step exists to catch.
3. ASSERT THE MUTATION LANDED by sha256: pre != post. A mutation that never applied and a mutation that failed to red share an exit code.

4. ASSERT THE MUTANT STILL CHECKS/BUILDS before reading any test result: check.passed still true for AILANG arms, go vet clean for Go arms. 'The mutant does not compile' is a third fact wearing the same exit code as 'the mutant was killed'. For MU5/MU6 this is inverted deliberately: their EXPECTED observable is verify.errors==1 with check.passed still true - record both fields.

5. READ THE SCOPED OBSERVABLE, NEVER THE EXIT CODE. For test arms, parse the JSON and print the LIST of non-pass identities - the ACs require the named test to be the SOLE failure, which a suite-wide red/green cannot show. For Go arms use -run '<TestName>' and read the t.Fatalf message text.

6. RESTORE BY cp FROM /tmp/w15_backup/ - NEVER 'git checkout -- <file>'. The worktree files are uncommitted by construction during M2; git checkout -- would destroy the executor's work and then report the disaster rather than prevent it. Assert byte-identical by sha256.
7. Re-run the positive control and require GREEN before the next arm.

issues_to_file.title: v0.30.0: a record containing a bare ADT field is Z3-unencodable and fails silently at rc level
issues_to_file.body_must_contain: Repro: a record type with an ADT-typed field, contract on the record parameter. Observed: check.passed=true, rc 0, verify.errors=1, 'Z3 error ... unknown sort <T>'. Same-shape control: the flat int record verifies with errors=0. Note this is STRICTER than the previously recorded list[ADT] limitation - the list is not needed, the bare ADT field alone fails.

issues_to_file.title: v0.30.0: inline-test harness cannot execute tuple-valued inputs (collected, then 'no pattern matched')
issues_to_file.body_must_contain: Multi-argument tests [...] rows fail to PARSE. Tuple-valued inputs are COLLECTED and then fail at runtime with 'no pattern matched in match expression', in BOTH nested-match and direct tuple-pattern forms.

issues_to_file.title: v0.30.0: ADT equality in a general boolean expression needs an Eq instance; the suggested 'import std/prelude' workaround is unsupported
issues_to_file.body_must_contain: 'No instance for Eq[<T>] in scope. Equality (==, !=) needs an Eq instance' at the ADT-equality site inside a conjunction. The error's own suggested fix, import std/prelude, fails with IMP012_UNSUPPORTED_NAMESPACE ... namespace imports not yet supported. The top-level 'result == match ...' postcondition form DOES verify - which is what forces a three-law split instead of one combined validTimeout law.
